cls: Vinca alkaloid derivative (cerebral vasodilator / PDE1 inhibitor)
quick: 5-10 mg orally three times daily (typical; per regional product)
Take with food to improve absorption
Avoid - not recommended; FDA warns against use in pregnancy
Limited data; caution in significant impairment
Blood pressure; bleeding signs if on antiplatelet/anticoagulant
summary: Vinpocetine is a semisynthetic derivative of the vinca alkaloid vincamine, marketed in some countries as a prescription drug for cerebrovascular disorders and cognitive impairment, and sold elsewhere (including the US) as a dietary supplement. It is thought to improve cerebral blood flow and have neuroprotective and PDE1-inhibitory actions. Evidence of clinical benefit is limited, it is not FDA-approved, and the FDA has warned that it may be unsafe in pregnancy.
indications: Cerebrovascular disorders and their sequelae (e.g., post-stroke, vascular cognitive symptoms) - where approved
Symptoms of chronic cerebral circulatory insufficiency
Adjunct for memory and cognitive complaints (supplement use, evidence limited)

dosage.n: Per regional product; commonly 15-30 mg/day total

admin: Take with or after food to enhance absorption
Follow the specific product or prescriber instructions, as formulations and strengths vary by country
Do not use if pregnant or trying to conceive
moa: Vinpocetine is proposed to act through several mechanisms: selective inhibition of phosphodiesterase type 1 (PDE1) raising cyclic nucleotide levels, blockade of voltage-gated sodium channels, enhancement of cerebral blood flow and microcirculation, improved oxygen and glucose utilization by neural tissue, and antioxidant/neuroprotective effects. The clinical relevance of these mechanisms is not firmly established.

absolute: Pregnancy (FDA warning - may harm the fetus / cause miscarriage)
relative: Concurrent anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy (possible increased bleeding)
Significant arrhythmia or unstable cardiovascular disease
monitor: Signs of bleeding when combined with anticoagulants/antiplatelets

preg: Avoid in pregnancy. The US FDA has warned that vinpocetine may decrease fetal weight or cause miscarriage and advises that women who are pregnant or who could become pregnant should not take it.
lact: There is insufficient information on use during breastfeeding; avoid because safety has not been established.
renal: Data in renal impairment are limited; use with caution.
hepatic: Data in hepatic impairment are limited; use with caution in significant liver disease.

moderate: Anticoagulants (warfarin) and antiplatelet agents (aspirin, clopidogrel) - possible increased bleeding tendency
minor: Other nootropics or vasoactive agents (additive effects, limited data)
interactions.food: Taking with food improves bioavailability; no clinically significant adverse food interaction
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; moderation advised

monitoring: Blood pressure, particularly at higher doses
Signs of bleeding if used with anticoagulants or antiplatelet drugs
counsel: This product is sold as a supplement in some countries and is not FDA-approved as a medicine
Do not use if you are pregnant, may become pregnant, or are breastfeeding
Take it with food to help absorption
Tell your doctor if you take blood thinners or have heart or blood-pressure problems
Report unusual bruising, bleeding, dizziness, or fainting
pk: Plasma levels rise within ~1 hour; clinical effects gradual
Peak plasma concentration about 1-1.5 hours after an oral dose
Short - approximately 1-2 hours (metabolite apovincaminic acid somewhat longer)
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved as a drug; in the US it is sold as a dietary supplement, while it is a prescription medicine for cerebrovascular disorders in several other countries (data from EMA/regional SmPC and BNF-type sources)
The FDA has specifically warned that vinpocetine may be unsafe in pregnancy (risk of reduced fetal weight or miscarriage)
Clinical efficacy evidence for cognition is limited and inconsistent
May add to the effect of anticoagulants/antiplatelets - watch for bleeding
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it and continue as usual - do not take a double dose.
overdose: Specific human overdose data are limited; expected effects relate to vasodilation and hypotension (dizziness, flushing, fainting) and gastrointestinal upset. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with monitoring of blood pressure and heart rhythm.
